      "explanation": "The refrain extends acknowledged justifications for some evils toward unexplained cases, potentially replacing the missing bridge between possibility and plausibility. Its repetition at E944–948 belongs to this episode; later limits at E2707–2714 prevent a clear unrestricted-protection finding."
    },
    {

      "quote": "but if god does exist it just turns out the evils are only apparently gratuitous",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "none"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "A conditionally reverses the argument and invokes unlimited divine knowledge, potentially absorbing unexplained suffering without identifying its justification. This is an ordinary conditional argument, supported by his earlier positive case, not a slogan. E1111–1124 adds specific goods; E2707–2714 and E3219–3224 later identify limits, leaving unrestricted protection uncertain."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2208,
      "endEvent": 2233,
      "contextStartEvent": 2184,
      "contextEndEvent": 2272,

      "quote": "and so you do have that",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",

      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "A interprets B's moral zeal as an unrecognized relationship with God, potentially neutralizing B's reported absence of that relationship. He supplies a scriptural interpretation and observed conduct at E2208–2221, but does not establish that these constitute divine contact. His personal, qualified wording and lack of an every-outcome rule make protection uncertain."
    },

      "form": "yes",

      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The catchphrase suggests intellectual sophistication can produce error, but no particular faulty inference by the sincere seeker is identified. It could substitute dismissal for examining that inquiry. Yet A describes a possibility, rejects anti-intellectualism at E2544–2545, and denies damnation for mere cognitive error at E2611–2619; disagreement is not unequivocally made proof of defect."
    }
